solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Might one make a little lunch efficiently? (4)

definitions.text: Might one make a little lunch efficiently?

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is taken, a little of them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words

annotation.surface: A question about who could knock up a quick lunch without fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight, it asks who might make lunch efficiently, and the professional cook is the natural reply.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a professional cook, whose job is turning out meals quickly and well.

entries.clue: Tile floor in bathroom, accomplishin’ nothing outside (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry the floor of a word is its bottom letter
the other pieces stand outside, wrapping round the floor letter

blocks.note: doing, with the G dropped as the apostrophe shows

annotation.surface: Someone lounging on the bathroom floor while the tiling sits undone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes tile and floor a bathroom job; tile is the definition, and floor, in a down clue, means the bottom letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Each piece in the game of dominoes is a small oblong tile marked with spots.

entries.clue: Special agents with it, most sharp (8)

indicators.note: something special is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their ordinary order

annotation.surface: Praise for an elite team of spies who are the sharpest going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Special agents' reads as one phrase, the FBI's kind; split it, and Special is the indicator acting on the next word plus it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the taste sense: a tangy flavour is sharp, like lemon.

entries.clue: I see love in abridged novel, alas and alack! (3-3)

indicators.note: the exclamation and love are put in, inside the shortened novel
an abridged book is cut short, so its last letter goes

annotation.surface: A reader lamenting that the love story they fancied has been cut down.
annotation.walkthrough: Novel here is just a book, with no hint of a particular title; the sad surface quietly matches the answer's sobbing.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are cries of lament, one old-fashioned and one mock-childish sobbing.

entries.clue: Fold and lift up thick biscuit (8)

blocks.note: a folded-over piece, as on an envelope
as you raise a car to change a wheel

annotation.surface: Instructions for handling dough or packaging a thick biscuit.
annotation.walkthrough: The British sense is meant, a chewy oat bar, not the American pancake of the same name.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Britain the word names a dense bar of oats, butter and syrup, a thick biscuit.

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A history note about an island that suffered a foreign occupation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true history: the island was occupied by Japan in the Second World War.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: it is the third-largest island in the world, in South-East Asia.

annotation.surface: A spy's anxious aside about keeping the network secret.
annotation.walkthrough: Network sounds like a ring of spies whose secret mustn't be told; it is the definition, meaning a web of threads.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: interlaced threads or wires form a network.

entries.clue: It’s tricky to handle this stew, small amount unfinished (3,6)

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its last letter

blocks.note: a Lancashire stew of meat baked under sliced potatoes

annotation.surface: A cook warning that a steaming stew is awkward to carry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This' in the wordplay points the stew at the answer itself, and the stew in question is a British dish baked under potato slices.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for an issue too awkward to deal with, taken from something literally too hot to hold.

indicators.note: a fanciful version is an imaginative reworking, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A remark about a paper whose proposition is growing more far-fetched.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece 'on' another sits above it; Article looks like a written paper but is the grammatical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proposition is a statement to be proved, which is the technical word here.

entries.clue: Wanton ladies and gentlemen, chaste finally (5)

indicators.note: the final letter of chaste

blocks.note: the Ladies and the Gents are both public toilets

annotation.surface: A disapproving verdict on a crowd that behaved wantonly before being chaste at last.
annotation.walkthrough: Ladies and gentlemen reads as people, but here they are the Ladies and the Gents; loo is British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned sense: a loose woman or loose morals were wanton, sexually unrestrained.

entries.clue: A bit short, and being tweaked? (7,3,5)

blocks.note: literally, having your skin squeezed between finger and thumb

annotation.surface: Someone a little short of cash who is also being tweaked.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: a tweak is a pinch; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for struggling financially, and a literal description of being tweaked.

entries.clue: Lines read in poem by nipper recalled (7)

indicators.note: called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a crab nips with its claws; CRAB turned round

annotation.surface: A child reciting lines of a poem from memory.
annotation.walkthrough: Nipper looks like a child reciting a poem, and nipper is British slang for a small child; here it is the creature that nips.
annotation.definitionFit: The striped code on goods is a set of printed lines that a scanner reads.

blocks.note: the usual short name for Buckinghamshire, an English county
American slang for dollars; abroad points overseas

annotation.surface: A tax note about a county's income earned overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: Revenue suggests the taxman; abroad is only there to send you to American money slang.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbreviated county name, and US slang for money.

entries.clue: In the zone where margarine might go? (2,1,4)

blocks.note: spread on a small bread bun

annotation.surface: A spread's-eye puzzle about where margarine ends up.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is literal, the place you spread margarine; the question mark admits the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a winning streak, and a literal spot for margarine.

entries.clue: Drink, second of the two unfinished (5)

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its last letter

blocks.note: the word for the second of two things, without its R

annotation.surface: Someone choosing the second of two drinks and leaving it half drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the second of two drinks the thing unfinished; really the word 'latter' is cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a milky espresso coffee is a drink.

entries.clue: Celestial body, if not OK, hit rocks by the way (4,2,5,2,2)

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about

blocks.note: a heavenly body with a tail

annotation.surface: A comet that, if it goes wrong, hits rocks along its path.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocks looks like the asteroids a stray comet might hit; it is the verb, shaking up the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are conversational asides introducing an afterthought.

entries.clue: Real book, one turned up in jumble (8)

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read upwards
the reversed pair goes inside the jumble word

blocks.note: B for book and I for one, turned upward

annotation.surface: A real book that has turned up among a jumble sale's stock.
annotation.walkthrough: Jumble looks like an anagram indicator, or a jumble sale where books turn up; it is a plain synonym and the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what can be touched is real and concrete.

indicators.note: something treated is processed and changed, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: An example of a skin complaint going untreated.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'for example' one phrase trailing the acne; the definition is example alone, with 'for' as the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a case in point, as in 'for instance'.

blocks.note: designated to, as in a job for someone

annotation.surface: A king's ransom set aside for music.
annotation.walkthrough: A king's ransom is an idiom for a huge sum; the surface pictures a monarch lavishing money on music.
annotation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean a vast sum of money.

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters are messed up

annotation.surface: A complaint that the conference is still a disorganised mess.
annotation.walkthrough: Remains reads as the verb, the conference is still a shambles; it is the noun, the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a meeting for discussion or training.

blocks.note: literally, produce the object named by 'that thing'

annotation.surface: A factory slogan about building a winning product.
annotation.walkthrough: Triumph could suggest the British car and motorbike maker, which is why manufacture follows.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for succeeding, and a literal instruction to produce something.

blocks.note: head up to bed for the night

annotation.surface: A choice between stepping downstairs or going upstairs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets down against up, yet both lead to the same word: leave office, or go up to bed.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of withdrawing: from work, and to bed.

indicators.note: about means around, so the payment goes round right

blocks.note: a group of things that belong together

annotation.surface: A courier to deliver a collection once payment is sorted.
annotation.walkthrough: Deliver reads as a courier's job; here it means release, as in 'deliver us from evil'.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: to deliver a captive is to release them.

indicators.note: the letters are in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A recount after a wrong vote tally in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an election miscount; the city is in Arizona.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a city in southern Arizona.

blocks.note: literally, what a bank does with money paid in

annotation.surface: A bank clerk weighing up a deposit.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal banking; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for weighing something up, and a literal description of banking a deposit.

blocks.note: not the painter but anything that turns
not paintings but the coloured waters of the sea

annotation.surface: A note on the painter J. M. W. Turner's watercolours.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner is the English painter famous for seascapes and watercolours; read literally, the turner in the sea's waters is the ebb and flow that turns twice a day.
annotation.definitionFit: The sea's rise and fall 'turns' at high and low water, so it is a turner in the waters.

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words

blocks.note: the last letter of fact and the first three of eating

annotation.surface: An exclamation about a feeder actually eating.
annotation.walkthrough: Feeder sounds like a creature eating; it is the thing a young animal feeds from.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a young animal or baby feeds from it.

blocks.note: the boring tool needs a bit fitted to work

annotation.surface: A workout that needs a little something extra.
annotation.walkthrough: Bit reads as a small amount; here it is the steel piece that bores the hole.
annotation.definitionFit: Military practice routine, and the power tool that takes a bit.

entries.clue: Vacuous clerk read through review of a poorer musical show (4,5)

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides
one thing through another is set inside it
a review reworks and reconsiders, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: A dim clerk reading a review that calls a musical poorer.
annotation.walkthrough: Read through looks like the clerk reading a review; it is the container instruction, and review works on the two words that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a musical drama sung in rock style, such as Tommy.
